payload.title: Approval service: changesets, async jobs, policies and audit

payload.text: Async approval id for MCP polling

payload.cmd: cd code && cargo test -p rbc-ai approvals
payload.name: approvals

payload.note: Schema v6 adds tool, summary and expires to ai_approvals (ALTER TABLE, so a v5 database keeps its rows) with create_ai_approval, ai_approval, ai_approvals(status), resolve_ai_approval (UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending', returning the row it actually moved) and expire_ai_approvals(now). crates/ai/src/approval.rs: Changeset carries summary, BoardChange{before, after, expected_revision, action} for board content, one line per differing field (moves/arrows/circles/annotations/notes) and the arguments the approved call is replayed with; ApprovalStore enforces pending -> approved|denied|expired, refusing a second answer as AlreadyResolved(status) and an answer past the deadline as Expired (which also expires the row), with pending(now) sweeping due requests first, status(id) for MCP polling, and a 15-minute default TTL. audit is the queue row itself: status plus created/resolved/expires. Auto-approval stays in policy: a granted scope means the call never becomes a request, which the tests assert by finding no pending row after an auto-approved move. Agent loop: ToolHost::request_approval (default None, so no host is forced to have a queue) is called on RequiresApproval, the returned id goes into the tool result data and into the ApprovalRequired event, and the call is never executed. Server: SessionHost::request_approval loads the board and queues the reviewed call; GET /api/ai/approvals, GET /api/ai/approvals/{id}, POST /api/ai/approvals/{id}/approve and /deny answer 404 for an unknown id and 400 naming the reason for a lost race. Evidence: cargo test -p rbc-ai --all-features approvals -> 12 tests (changeset shape and round trip, pending is pollable, approve/deny, no second answer, expiry at the deadline, the sweep, oldest-first pending, unknown id, and three bypass cases: an ungranted write never reaches the board, a granted scope creates no request, an MCP call cannot borrow the in-app grant). Live over HTTP: play e4 queued one request with its arguments and 900000 ms deadline, board stayed at revision 1, approve set approved with a timestamp, a second approve was refused. NOT yet done, and t-4bfb's job: approving marks the request approved but does not replay the write; the changeset stores the arguments so the UI/service can execute exactly what was reviewed. The changeset's 'after' is the current board until a dry-run path for each write tool exists.
